author: fw-bot
body:
### Issue:
Due to this issue, `coupon_ids` which are never used are still shown in loyalty coupons history which is confusing for users.

#### Steps to reproduce:
1- Create two promotions:
   - Promo A: 10% discount
   - Promo B: 20% discount

2- Create a SO and add a line. Then confirm the SO.
3- Click on `Reward` button.
4- A dialog should show both promos. Discard the dialog.
5- Navigate to `Discount and Loyalty`.
6- Open Promo A and B and you can see both have lines with
   `coupon_id.order_id` = `created SO` which is confusing. `Issue 1`
7- Navigate back to SO. Click on `Reward` and select Promo A, apply.
8- Navigate to Promo B. As you see the the `coupon_id` related to
   the SO is still there. `Issue 2`

### Cause and Fix:
This is due to unlinking `coupon_ids` only in SO confirm action, causing this issue on already confirmed SOs:
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/604d07ab324caa5f3aa6f3baa9902c2137ea24db/addons/sale_loyalty/models/sale_order.py#L132-L136

We can fix this issue by `unlinking` the `coupons_ids` when a reward is applied or the dialog is discarded.

However there are 2 limitations:
1- The view needs to be updated. Otherwise, `coupon_ids` will not be deleted upon clicking on `discard` button. However the fix is still stable.
2- What if the dialog is closed with the cross button or the tab is closed without selecting a reward? In that case the issue will still persist.

To fix these issues, we can show only used `coupon_ids` in `loyalty_coupon_id` list view. However that cannot be done in stable as it requires `use_count` to be stored.
NB: With some complex filters this also could be fixed on stable but not worth it.

author: mrdnctrk
body:
Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  Added a new versionPolicy parameter to PackageInstallationSpec that controls how resource versions are handled during package installation in STORE_AND_INSTALL mode.                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  ### Background                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  When installing FHIR packages using STORE_AND_INSTALL mode, users need flexibility in how resources (StructureDefinitions, ValueSets, etc.) are installed. Some use cases require multiple versions of the same profile to   
  coexist (for multi-version validation), while others need a single authoritative version that gets updated when new packages are installed.                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  ### Changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  New versionPolicy Parameter                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  Two policies are now available:                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  - MULTI_VERSION (default): Uses server-assigned IDs for new resources. Existing resources are matched by both canonical URL and version. This allows multiple versions of the same profile to coexist in the repository.            
  - SINGLE_VERSION: Uses client-assigned IDs from the package. Existing resources are matched by canonical URL only (version is ignored). Installing a new version of a profile will overwrite the existing one.                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  Note: SearchParameter resources always use client-assigned IDs regardless of the versionPolicy setting, as only one version of a SearchParameter can exist per URL + base combination.                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  Implementation Details                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  - Added VersionPolicyEnum to PackageInstallationSpec                                                                                                                                                                                
  - Refactored PackageInstallerSvcImpl.createOrUpdateResource() for clarity, as it was too convoluted. I split into multiple methods.                                                                                                                                                           
  - Search queries now include _sort=_pid:desc for deterministic resource selection when multiple versions exist                                                                                                                      
  - meta.source is now set for all package resources regardless of version policy, as this shows from which package and version a resource came from.                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  Migration Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  The current default behavior (MULTI_VERSION) is preserved, so shouldn't be considered a breaking change.      


closes: https://github.com/hapifhir/hapi-fhir/issues/7512

- **Security**: Added `escapeXml()` to sanitize all content against injection (handles `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`)

## Before/After

```diff
- ---
- 
- Getting Started
- URL: https://example.com/getting-started
+ <document title="Getting Started" path="https://example.com/getting-started">
  Description: Learn how to get started
  
  Content here...
+ </document>
```

This improves machine parseability for LLM consumption while preventing malformed XML from user content.

author: dherman
body:
## Summary

This RFD proposes a `thinkwell` CLI and Bun plugin for automatic JSON Schema generation from TypeScript types, enabling a zero-configuration scripting experience.

### The Vision

```typescript
#!/usr/bin/env thinkwell

/** @JSONSchema */
interface Greeting {
  message: string;
}

// Greeting.Schema appears automatically - no build step needed
const result = await agent.think(Greeting.Schema).text("Hi").run();
```

### Key Design Decisions

- **`thinkwell` CLI as primary UX**: Wraps Bun with the plugin pre-configured
- **Bun `onLoad` hook**: Intercepts TypeScript files and injects namespace declarations
- **TypeScript Compiler API**: Provides type information (works with future tsgo)
- **ts-json-schema-generator**: Handles schema extraction

### Open Questions

1. Should the plugin work in production builds, or recommend build tool for prod?
2. How to handle schema generation errors (fail fast vs. warn)?
3. Future CLI commands (`thinkwell build`, `thinkwell init`)?

See [doc/rfd/bun-schema-plugin.md](doc/rfd/bun-schema-plugin.md) for the full proposal.

author: danielsjoo
body:
Dockerized the keepid_server development environment. This setup allows you to run the application and its database (MongoDB) without installing Java or MongoDB locally. This makes the server possible to run without intellij, and onboarding (especially between mac/windows environments) easier.

Requires: Docker Desktop and gitignored .env file

**Start the Server:**
```
docker-compose up --build
```
The server will start on http://localhost:7001
MongoDB will leverage the mongo-data volume for persistence.

**Remote Debugging:**
Port 5005 is exposed.
Connect your IDE (IntelliJ/Eclipse) to localhost:5005 with a "Remote JVM Debug" configuration.

**Database Connection:** 
The app connects to mongo staging-db

**Portability:**
Migration: You can deploy this Dockerfile to any cloud provider that supports Docker (AWS ECS, Google Cloud Run, Azure Container Apps, DigitalOcean, etc.).
Dependencies: While the compute is portable, you will still need to configure external services (GCP KMS, SendGrid/Lob, etc.) via environment variables in the new provider.

**Java Version**

This docker uses  maven:3.9.6-eclipse-temurin-21 version of java. The non-alpine version is important for making argon2 password hashing work on non Windows devices. The `eclipse-temurin:21-jre` image is multi-arch and Docker automatically selects the correct architecture.

The new Dockerfile works on any OS (mac and windows need docker desktop).

Other tradeoffs of this version:
- Image size - Debian-based images are larger (~200MB vs ~50MB for Alpine), but provide better compatibility with Java native libraries
- Security - Alpine is known for minimal attack surface, but Debian images are regularly updated and patched

body: Damn this repo is on 🔥 ! Sooo.. Finally had a bit of time to look at this idea. I went a bit back and forward on it, and for now I believe the original idea works best, which is simply to trigger the highlight on "?". This goes well with the `` element usage, and is a really simple approach. I think it works really well in dark mode, less well in light mode (see the video). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ef5c626-3253-484e-be9f-c6c8796d624d @danielroe you also proposed to trigger the highlight on any key-press that isn't already bound to something. What gives me pause about that feature is that it reminds me about clicking in the wrong spot in a Figma prototype. Enough for me to prefer the original over it. What works well with that idea is that it makes it possible to "stumble over" an otherwise somewhat hidden feature - something my original idea doesn't really solve. I also played around with a variant that opens a small section at the bottom, and lists the keyboard shortcuts available in the current view. Ultimately that idea falls on its face for two reasons: it collides with the footer and we just don't have that many shortcuts right now (4 at most) - though you could add other tips to the section "did you know.." style or whatever. **I'm happy to get feedback on this, and I'm also happy pursue another direction, or put it on ice for now 😄** closes https://github.com/npmx-dev/npmx.dev/pull/461

author: gvcutv
body:
### Motivation
- The ETL-derived stage-duration outputs were labeled as `avg_wait_*` which conflated queue-wait and service-time semantics.  The validation workflow needs explicit service-time baselines to compare against per-ticket `service_time_*` produced by the simulator. 
- Validation checks and documentation must reflect that ETL phase durations are used as coarse service-time baselines (and that queue-length proxies remain computed with Little’s Law). 

### Description
- Renamed the ETL baseline metric emitted by `validation/baseline_extract.py` from `avg_wait_{stage}` to `avg_service_time_{stage}` and updated the metric note to indicate it is a service-time baseline.
- Updated `validation/checks.py` so `check_baseline` will source `avg_service_time_*` observations from per-ticket aggregates when `ticket_rows` are available by adding handling for metrics that start with `avg_service_time_`.
- Added computation of per-stage service-time means to `aggregate_ticket_means` in `validation/checks.py`, emitting `avg_service_time_dev`, `avg_service_time_review`, and `avg_service_time_testing` keys derived from `service_time_*` fields in ticket rows.
- Revised `docs/validation/validation_plan.md` to map `avg_service_time_*` to ETL phase durations and updated the acceptance criteria wording to refer to service-time baselines and their ±20% tolerance.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.

author: forketyfork
body:
## Summary
- Enhance human-readable text output with source line display and caret pointers
- Extract console and SARIF formatters into separate modules
- Add new `sentinel-alloc` rule to detect sentinel-terminated allocation bugs
- Fix memory mismatch bugs in file content caching

## Changes

### Text Output Enhancement
- Updated diagnostic output to show the actual source line with a caret-style pointer under the problematic span
- Added in-memory file cache to prevent repeated file reads when printing multiple diagnostics for the same file

### Formatter Extraction
- Extracted `ConsoleFormatter` to `src/formatters/console.zig`
- Extracted `SarifFormatter` to `src/formatters/sarif.zig`

### New Rule: `sentinel-alloc`
Warns about functions that create sentinel-terminated allocations, which can cause memory mismatch bugs if the sentinel type information is lost:

| Function | Sentinel Behavior | Warning Condition |
|----------|-------------------|-------------------|
| `readToEndAllocOptions` | Optional (5th param) | When sentinel is non-null |
| `allocWithOptions` | Optional (4th param) | When sentinel is non-null |
| `allocSentinel` | Always | Always warns |
| `dupeZ` | Always (null-terminated) | Always warns |
| `allocPrintSentinel` | Always | Always warns |

**The bug pattern detected:**
```zig
// 1. Create sentinel allocation → [:0]u8 (allocates len+1)
const s = allocator.dupeZ(u8, "hello");

// 2. Store in non-sentinel type → []const u8 (type info LOST)
cache.put(key, s);  

// 3. Free through non-sentinel type → frees len bytes (WRONG!)
allocator.free(cache.get(key));  // Should free len+1!
```

### Bug Fixes
- `console.zig`: Changed `readToEndAllocOptions` sentinel from `0` to `null` (sentinel not needed)
- `analyzer.zig`: Fixed sentinel allocation free to use `ptr[0..len+1]` to include sentinel byte
- `sarif.zig`: Removed unused `std` import

## Test Plan
- [x] `just test` passes
- [x] `just lint` passes
- [x] Added test fixtures for sentinel-alloc rule:
  - `detects_non_null_sentinel.zig`
  - `detects_dupe_z.zig`
  - `detects_alloc_sentinel.zig`
  - `allows_null_sentinel.zig`

author: johnie
body:
## What

Improves the OAuth2 authentication experience by implementing an automatic local callback server, eliminating the need to manually copy authorization codes from the browser.

## Why

The previous authentication flow required users to:
1. Open the auth URL manually
2. Authorize the application
3. Get redirected to a localhost URL that shows "connection refused"
4. Manually copy the authorization code from the URL
5. Paste it back into the terminal

This was error-prone and confusing for users. The new flow handles everything automatically.

## How

- Implements a local HTTP server using Bun.serve() that listens for the OAuth callback
- Auto-opens the browser on supported platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows)
- Displays styled HTML pages for success/error states
- Detects headless environments (CI, SSH) and adjusts behavior
- Adds `--manual` flag to fall back to the old copy-paste workflow
- Introduces `normalizeRedirectUri` helper to handle redirect URIs without explicit ports

## Changes

- Add local OAuth callback server with 2-minute timeout
- Add styled HTML success/error pages with monospace design
- Add cross-platform browser opening (open/xdg-open/cmd start)
- Add headless environment detection
- Add `normalizeRedirectUri` function for handling port-less redirect URIs
- Add `redirectUriOverride` parameter to `createOAuth2Client`
- Add `-m`/`--manual` flag to auth CLI command
- Update code style docs to prefer interface over type for object types

## Testing

- [x] Manual testing completed on macOS
- [x] Tested `--manual` fallback mode
- [x] Tested timeout behavior
- [x] Tested error handling (access denied, etc.)

author: jhuesing
body:
Fixes #4826

## Problem

The cron documentation shows CLI usage examples but lacks JSON schema for programmatic tool calls, forcing users to guess at field names and structure.

### What I tried (wrong):
```json
{
  "schedule": {"in": "30m"},        // ❌ doesn't exist
  "payload": {"message": "..."},   // ❌ wrong field
  "sessionTarget": {"kind": "current"} // ❌ should be string
}
```

### What actually works:
```json
{
  "name": "reminder-name",
  "schedule": {"kind": "at", "atMs": 1738262400000},
  "sessionTarget": "main",
  "payload": {"kind": "systemEvent", "text": "Reminder text"},
  "wakeMode": "now",
  "deleteAfterRun": true
}
```

## Solution

Added comprehensive JSON schema section to `/automation/cron-jobs.md` with:

### New sections added:
- **Common Fields** - All job properties (name, schedule, sessionTarget, agentId, deleteAfterRun)
- **Schedule Kinds** - Complete documentation of `at`, `every`, and `cron` schedules
- **Payloads** - Both `systemEvent` (main session) and `agentTurn` (isolated session)
- **Delivery Options** - Channel delivery configuration for isolated jobs
- **Telegram Topics** - Forum topic delivery format with examples

### Key documentation:
- **atMs validation**: Clarified that this is epoch milliseconds, not ISO string
- **Schedule patterns**: Concrete examples for one-shot, interval, and cron expressions
- **Field mapping**: Tables showing field types, requirements, and descriptions
- **Consistency**: All JSON examples match existing CLI examples

## Impact
- **Developers**: Can now integrate cron jobs programmatically without guessing
- **Sub-agents**: Clear schema for calling cron tool from spawned sessions
- **Accuracy**: Reduces field name errors (schedule.in vs schedule.kind, etc.)

Fixes #4826

author: copilot
body:
`ManipulationAbsolute` controls world-space vs object-space manipulation. It was only implemented for 3D entities (via ImGuizmo's `MODE.WORLD`/`MODE.LOCAL`). 2D entity dragging always operated in world space.

## Changes

- **2D position drag**: Added conditional transform based on `ManipulationAbsolute` flag
  - When `true`: World space manipulation (existing behavior)
  - When `false`: Object space manipulation by rotating mouse delta through entity's inverse rotation

```fsharp
let entityPosition =
    if ManipulationAbsolute then
        // world space
        (entityDragOffset - mousePositionWorldOriginal) + (mousePositionWorld - mousePositionWorldOriginal)
    else
        // object space - transform mouse delta to entity's local coordinates
        let mouseDelta = mousePositionWorld - mousePositionWorldOriginal
        let entityDegrees = if entity.MountExists world then (entity.GetDegreesLocal world).Z else (entity.GetDegrees world).Z
        let entityRadians = degToRadF entityDegrees
        let mouseDeltaLocal = mouseDelta.Rotate -entityRadians
        (entityDragOffset - mousePositionWorldOriginal) + mouseDeltaLocal
```

The implementation transforms the world-space mouse delta into the entity's local coordinate frame by rotating it by `-θ` where `θ` is the entity's Z-axis rotation. This matches the 3D manipulation's local mode semantics.

1. **Due Date Parsing**: The `--due` parameter now accepts:
   - ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD)
   - The keyword `tomorrow`
   - Relative dates in the format `+Nd`

2. **Task Sorting**: The task list is sorted such that:
   - Tasks with due dates appear first, sorted by date.
   - Tasks without due dates appear at the end of the list.

3. **Tests**: Updated and added tests to cover new due date formats and sorting behavior.

author: marcqualie
body:
## Summary

- Remove `.strict()` from Zod config schemas (`ProjectConfigSchema`) to allow forward compatibility
- Older Denvig versions now gracefully ignore unknown config properties added by newer versions
- VSCode JSON Schema validation still warns about unknown properties via `additionalProperties: false` (hardcoded in codegen)

## Problem

When running two versions of Denvig simultaneously (e.g., production + local test build), configs with new properties would cause parsing failures. The production version's `strict()` Zod validation would reject unknown properties, resulting in empty configs.

## Solution

Removed `.strict()` from three locations in `src/schemas/config.ts`:
- The `http` object in service config
- The service object itself
- The root `ProjectConfigSchema`

This gives:
- **Runtime**: Lenient parsing - unknown properties are silently stripped (Zod's default behavior)
- **VSCode**: Strict validation - unknown properties show as warnings via JSON Schema

## Test plan

- [x] All tests pass (`pnpm run test`)
- [x] Codegen regenerates schemas successfully
- [x] JSON schema still has `additionalProperties: false` (4 occurrences)
- [x] CLI works correctly with configs containing unknown properties
- [x] Production build successful

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> The GitHub Actions workflow is failing with the following error when running pytest:
> 
> ```
> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'board'
> ```
> 
> This occurs in `tests/test_main_volume.py` when it imports `main`, which in turn imports `firmware/circuitpython/main.py`. That file imports CircuitPython-specific hardware modules (`board`, `busio`) that are not available in standard Python environments used by CI.
> 
> **Failing job:** https://github.com/bwedderburn/BM83-ESP32-S3-Nextion/actions/runs/21528633176/job/62041091259
> 
> **Error trace:**
> ```
> firmware/circuitpython/main.py:3: in <module>
>     import board
> E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'board'
> ```
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Mock the CircuitPython hardware modules at the top of `tests/test_main_volume.py` before importing `main`. This will allow tests to run in CI and local environments without requiring actual hardware or CircuitPython libraries.
> 
> ## Implementation
> 
> Add the following imports and mocks at the very top of `tests/test_main_volume.py` (before the existing imports):
> 
> ```python
> import sys
> from unittest import mock
> 
> # Mock CircuitPython modules for CI/testing
> sys.modules['board'] = mock.MagicMock()
> sys.modules['busio'] = mock.MagicMock()
> ```
> 
> This should be added before the existing `import types` and `import main` lines.
> 
> ## Expected Outcome
> 
> After this change, pytest should run successfully in GitHub Actions without the `ModuleNotFoundError`, allowing the test suite to execute properly.


</details>

This pull request introduces a foundational security and middleware framework to the application, focusing on authentication, authorization, and extensible request processing. It adds abstractions for user authentication, role-based access control, and a flexible system for "Givers" and "Middlewares" that can be injected and resolved dynamically. The changes also include supporting annotations and utility classes to enable these features, as well as integration with the application's scanning and initialization process.

**Authentication & Authorization Framework:**

- Introduced the `AuthUser` interface and its `AnonUser` implementation to represent authenticated and anonymous users, respectively. Also added an abstract `AbstractAuthGiver` class to encapsulate authentication logic and user extraction, including role checks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9d064e44b5e35a4d3d7b73d43da0c804b524f43b9ee183eb66e1320bebd433c2R1-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2f3cc47b84050a2881f94448fcd9edfc13c7fbcb64d33a56aa8c86f01a8e0105R1-R20) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8b153c7c79fb1f76d65434410f28ee1ecc478340c4a591228e0517e758bf7332R1-R62)
- Added `HasRole` and `Roles` annotations to support role-based method authorization, and created the `Authenticated` middleware to enforce authentication and role checks before controller execution. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6fcd99504ed17725a4a05e94f1dbee0088e2a2bb493d441fde30386d9738a788R1-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-38e4e3d3ec42c06e7564e8173695ed06fda4a6ea5bf882d913ea3368bbfd0457R1-R12) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-11d89ea6813a2d08673b4e1bad009d19dda1a47ea9fb04ab053572471e90a778R1-R45)
- Added a custom `UnauthorizedException` for handling unauthorized access in HTTP responses.

**Middleware and Giver Infrastructure:**

- Introduced the `Middleware` base class and its supporting annotations (`Middlewares`, `MiddlewareConfig`) to allow request pre- and post-processing via injectable middlewares. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f1388124cb85a36200d6e53d2fea9b71c750fbd5c127e42a4772627656d91196R1-R41) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1aeb25fb8b68307a92ef18ed6d202dd06f08db7f28639f51700fdb020f2d1e81R1-R20) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6204901fbd8fe26fc2833400b4e9103feeb9c364ebce88d5b73bdd1ad932db4fR1-R12)
- Added the `Giver` interface and `GiverConfig` annotation to enable dependency injection and dynamic resolution of pre-controller logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d3429939896f9bc58a60eae5b203b8155e7eb0309aacca2fb99140c72ccd9c6cR1-R45) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-753d4f152a6c00b199013706a31a500218500bcc31920c3d208c918153924ffaR1-R15)
- Implemented the `ResolvContainer` class to encapsulate method and annotation metadata for dynamic resolution.

**Framework Integration & Scanning Enhancements:**

- Updated the `App` class to scan and manage resolvable classes (Givers and Middlewares), and integrated these into the web request mapping and finding process. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-14abe86015eff61b3ad51189f18d7d38dcd5100f6094c9d137dbaa943a10ba28R10-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-14abe86015eff61b3ad51189f18d7d38dcd5100f6094c9d137dbaa943a10ba28R30-R39) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-14abe86015eff61b3ad51189f18d7d38dcd5100f6094c9d137dbaa943a10ba28R62) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-14abe86015eff61b3ad51189f18d7d38dcd5100f6094c9d137dbaa943a10ba28R86-R92) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-14abe86015eff61b3ad51189f18d7d38dcd5100f6094c9d137dbaa943a10ba28L85-R105)
- Added the `ScanResolvs` utility for discovering resolvable classes within a package, supporting extensibility for new Givers and Middlewares.

**Dependency Management:**

- Added the `byte-buddy` library to `pom.xml` to support runtime code generation and proxying, which is used for dynamic resolution and injection.

author: jacklionheart
body:
## Try it

Create a new wave in Concerto's sidebar. Instead of a disabled Start button, you'll see:

1. **AreaPicker** - select where to focus (recent areas, browse, or infer from branch changes)
2. **StepRunner** - run individual steps with direction pills and optional prompts
3. **TransitionBar** - appears after running steps, offering Set Stimulus / Create PR / Archive

Setting a stimulus transitions the wave to Conduct mode (autonomous operation).

## Summary

Improvise mode makes wave creation discoverable. Previously, creating a wave dumped you at an idle screen with no guidance. Now the UI adapts to wave state: unconfigured waves show area selection, configured-but-idle waves show the step runner, and running waves show the existing Conduct view.

Also adds macOS notifications for wave state changes (interactive steps waiting, errors, PR ready) so users know when waves need attention.

## Changes

- New Improvise components: AreaPicker, StepRunner, TransitionBar, DirectionPills
- RecentAreasService persists area selections per-repo in UserDefaults
- NotificationService sends local notifications on wave status transitions
- WaveDetailPanel state machine detects unconfigured vs improvise vs conduct views
- Direction model gets public initializer for previews
- Branch naming: `parse_branch_base` strips nested timestamps correctly

author: alexander-turner
body:
## Summary
This PR adds the `eslint-plugin-regexp` ESLint plugin and enforces the use of named capture groups in regular expressions across the codebase. This improves code readability and maintainability by making regex patterns more self-documenting.

## Key Changes

- **Added eslint-plugin-regexp dependency** (v3.0.0) to enforce regex best practices
- **Enabled `regexp/prefer-named-capture-group` rule** as an error in ESLint configuration
- **Converted all regex patterns** throughout the codebase to use named capture groups instead of positional indices:
  - Updated regex patterns in transformers (formatting, OFM, spoiler, subtitles, etc.)
  - Updated regex patterns in components (ContentMeta, TableOfContents, popover helpers, etc.)
  - Updated regex patterns in utilities and processors
  - Updated test files to use named groups
  
- **Updated regex replacement calls** to use named group syntax (`$<groupName>`) instead of positional references (`$1`, `$2`, etc.)
- **Updated match group access** from positional indices (`match[1]`, `match[2]`) to named group properties (`match.groups.groupName`)

## Notable Implementation Details

- Non-capturing groups `(?:...)` were used where capture groups weren't needed, reducing unnecessary captures
- All `RegExp.exec()` and `String.match()` calls were updated to safely access groups via `match?.groups`
- Regex replacement functions were updated to properly handle named groups, including those using `matchAll()` and `replaceAll()`
- The changes maintain backward compatibility while improving code clarity and reducing potential indexing errors

## Benefits

- **Improved readability**: Named groups make regex intent clearer
- **Reduced bugs**: Eliminates fragile positional index dependencies
- **Better maintainability**: Easier to understand and modify complex regex patterns
- **Consistent style**: Enforces a single regex pattern style across the entire codebase

author: robert-j-y
body:
## Description

Fixes #387

Adds support for setting default values for common model parameters at model creation time. Previously, settings like `temperature` could only be passed at call time via `generateText`/`streamText`. Now users can set defaults when creating the model:

```typescript
// Before: TypeScript error - temperature not allowed
const model = openrouter('google/gemini-3-flash-preview', {
  temperature: 0 // ❌ Error
});

// After: Works correctly
const model = openrouter('google/gemini-3-flash-preview', {
  temperature: 0,
  topP: 0.9,
  maxTokens: 100,
});
```

Call-level options still override model-level settings when provided.

### New settings added to `OpenRouterSharedSettings`:
- `temperature` - Controls randomness (0-2)
- `topP` - Nucleus sampling (0-1)
- `topK` - Top-k sampling
- `frequencyPenalty` - Penalize repeated tokens (-2 to 2)
- `presencePenalty` - Penalize tokens based on presence (-2 to 2)
- `maxTokens` - Maximum tokens to generate

### Key areas for review:
- Nullish coalescing (`??`) is used so call-level `undefined` falls back to model settings, but explicit values always win
- Both chat and completion models implement the same fallback logic
- Regression test uses exact code pattern from issue #387

body:
Hello, here's a working implementation of `splice!` for `CircularVectors`. 

The `AbstractUnitRange` method took reimplementing of Base.splice! internals. This is because simply putting in the modular range (`mod(first):mod(last)`  causes issues when first > last and first is length of the array+1. (in plain language, trying to splice a vector between the last and first elements).  Inputting the modular range will delete the entire array. Re-implementing, as I did, places the `ins` before the first element.

Maybe you have some clever simplification, but this was what I could figure out.

Geo tests were failing because Chrome's headless mode in CI lacks GPU hardware, causing WebGL initialization to fail for maplibre-gl map rendering.

body:
### Motivation
- Remove the intrusive wrong-answer modal and unify feedback into the existing HUD/judge flow to match the correct-answer UX. 
- Allow stages to run indefinitely (no automatic 30-question clear), and make the game continue and accelerate rather than forcing a finish BGM/clear at a fixed count. 
- Make lane height smaller so multiple lanes fit more compactly on small screens and increase spawn/speed aggressiveness for a faster, continuous challenge.

### Description
- Removed the wrong-answer modal markup and related UI APIs and event wiring so incorrect answers no longer open a separate modal (`index.html`, `ui/dom.js`).
- Switched miss handling to compute the correct label/explanation via `getCorrectInfoForQuestion` and surface miss feedback through the normal HUD/judge feedback instead of a modal (`engine/game.js`).
- Made stage `clearCount` infinite by setting `clearCount: Infinity` across stage definitions so stages do not auto-clear at 30 questions (`stages/*.js`) and updated HUD/result formatting to handle infinite clear counts (`ui/dom.js`, `engine/game.js`).
- Reduced minimum lane/card height and adjusted `setLaneHeight` calculation to use smaller base heights so lanes can be more compact (`ui/dom.js`, `style.css` small modal width tweak).
- Accelerated gameplay by lowering time limits and spawn intervals: reduced minimum `timeLimitSec` floors and lowered `calcSpawnIntervalSec` minimum, and removed a strict clamping step so pacing continues to speed up as intended (`engine/game.js`).
- Removed the normals toggle UI and its handlers to declutter the HUD (`index.html`, `ui/dom.js`, `main.js`).

### Testing
- Launched a local static server with `python -m http.server 8000` and exercised the UI with Playwright to capture a menu screenshot saved as `artifacts/menu-view.png`, which succeeded. 
- An automated Playwright attempt to click the stage button timed out while trying to capture an in-game screenshot, but a subsequent run produced the menu screenshot artifact above. 
- No unit tests were present or run; changes were validated via the manual/headless visual check described above.

author: tryuan99
body:
To be more explicit for the interceptor and threat events, this PR adds a new event called `INTERCEPTOR_DESTROYED` and `THREAT_DESTROYED`, which occur when agents are destroyed _prior_ to reaching their target.

* `INTERCEPTOR_HIT` denotes when an interceptor successfully hits its target.
* `INTERCEPTOR_MISS` denotes exclusively when an interceptor misses its target due to the kill probability.  This does not destroy the interceptor.
* `INTERCEPTOR_DESTROYED` denotes when an interceptor is destroyed prior to reaching its target, e.g., through a ground collision.
* `THREAT_HIT` denotes when a threat hits its target (the asset).
* `THREAT_DESTROYED` denotes when a threat is destroyed prior to reaching the asset, e.g., by being intercepted or colliding with the ground.

* `THREAT_MISS` has been removed because threats cannot miss their targets.

## Summary

Replaces various config string handlers with a new `ArgString` format. 

## Details

Replaces the dataset config parser with a more advance "arg_string" parser with support for nested and list config structures. For example:

```
prefix_buckets[0].bucket_weight=10,prefix_buckets[0].prefix_count=10,prefix_buckets[1].bucket_weight=20,prefix_buckets[1].prefix_count=4
```

Renders to

```python
{
    "prefix_buckets": [
        {"bucket_weight": 10, "prefix_count": 10},
        {"bucket_weight": 20, "prefix_count": 4},
     ]
}
```

Also added some glue logic to allow this format anywhere on the CLI that supports JSON. This code should be considered temporary as it will mostly be replaced through the rest of the CLI refactor.

Also open to suggestions for a better name then "arg_string"; a 2-4 letter acronym like JSON or YAML would be good.

author: mitmelon
body:
*   💡 **What:** Replaced the use of the blocking `KEYS` command in `RedisAdapter::query` with the non-blocking `SCAN` iterator. Added client-side deduplication to handle potential duplicates returned by `SCAN`.
*   🎯 **Why:** The `KEYS` command is O(N) where N is the total number of keys in the database. Executing it blocks the entire Redis server, which is dangerous in production environments with large datasets. `SCAN` allows incremental iteration, preventing blocking.
*   📊 **Measured Improvement:**
    *   **Baseline:** `Redis::keys` was confirmed to be called via a reproduction script. This operation is known to be blocking.
    *   **Improvement:** `Redis::scan` is now called iteratively. Verification scripts confirmed that the iteration logic is correct, covers all keys, and correctly filters duplicates. While exact timing benchmarks against a live production Redis are not available in this environment, the theoretical improvement shifts the complexity from a single O(N) blocking operation to multiple O(1) (approximate) non-blocking calls, which is the industry standard for production safety.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve rendering performance when the tree has a large number of visible rows by supporting virtualized row rendering with a UI-Scroll-backed viewport. 
- Provide a configurable, optional mode so existing behavior remains unchanged when virtual scrolling is not enabled.

### Description
- Added virtual scroll state and helpers to the TreeDnD controller including `$scope.virtualScrollEnabled`, `$scope.virtualScrollBuffer`, `$scope.virtualScrollRowHeight`, `$scope.virtualScrollViewportStyle`, `$scope.virtualScrollNodes`, an `adapter` object and a UI-Scroll `datasource` (`virtualScrollDatasource.get`). (`src/directive/angular-tree-dnd.js` and mirrored in `dist/*` bundles).
- Implemented `updateVirtualScrollNodes()` to maintain the visible-node list used by the datasource and call it after `reload_data()` so the virtual viewport stays in sync with tree visibility. (`src/directive/angular-tree-dnd.js`, `dist/*`).
- Added `initVirtualScrollSettings()` to read attributes (`virtual-scroll`, `virtual-scroll-buffer`, `virtual-scroll-row-height`, `virtual-scroll-height`) and populate scope settings; called at init. (`src/directive/angular-tree-dnd.js`, `dist/*`).
- Updated the default template to conditionally render either the regular full `tbody` or a UI-Scroll-backed `ui-scroll-viewport` `tbody` with `ui-scroll`, `adapter`, `buffer-size`, and `item-size` bindings. (`src/module/angular-tree-dnd-template.append.js` and `dist/*` templates).
- Added viewport styling `.tree-dnd-viewport` to the CSS and SCSS to make the scroll container layout predictable. (`src/ng-tree-dnd.scss`, `src/ng-tree-dnd.css`, and `dist/*` CSS outputs).
- Documented the new attributes in `DOCUMENTS.md` (`virtual-scroll`, `virtual-scroll-height`, `virtual-scroll-buffer`, `virtual-scroll-row-height`).
- Synchronized changes into distribution files under `dist/` so packaged builds include the feature and styles.

body:
## Summary
Refactored the codebase to extract Prisma-related types into a centralized `@/types/prisma` module, improving type safety and maintainability by reducing direct dependencies on `@prisma/client` imports across the application.

## Key Changes

- **Created centralized type definitions**: Introduced `@/types/prisma` module to house custom types like `Role`, `UserSearchResult`, `UserGrowthData`, and `UserGrowthResult`
- **Updated imports across server actions**: Modified `actions/account.ts`, `actions/admin.ts`, `actions/auth.ts`, and `actions/user-stats.ts` to import types from the new module instead of directly from `@prisma/client`
- **Enhanced type annotations**: Added explicit type annotations to callback functions in:
  - `actions/admin.ts`: Added `UserSearchResult` type to user mapping
  - `actions/user-stats.ts`: Added `UserGrowthData` type to destructured parameters
  - `components/pages/admin/UsersTable.tsx`: Added `UserSearchResult` type annotation
  - `components/pages/user/dashboard/Charts.tsx`: Added `UserGrowthResult` and `ChartData` type annotations
- **Improved date handling**: Refactored date formatting logic in `actions/account.ts` to use type guards and separate conditional branches for better clarity

## Benefits

- **Better separation of concerns**: Prisma types are now isolated from business logic
- **Improved type safety**: Explicit type annotations prevent runtime errors
- **Easier maintenance**: Centralized type definitions make future updates simpler
- **Reduced coupling**: Components and actions no longer directly depend on `@prisma/client` for type definitions

author: alan-jowett
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1080 - Service Bus SQL filter rules not applied after commit 3a44511c.

## Problem

The Bicep template named the SQL filter rules $Default intending to replace the auto-created TrueFilter. However:

1. Azure auto-creates a $Default TrueFilter when a subscription is created
2. ARM/Bicep trying to create another $Default rule fails silently
3. Subscriptions end up with **no rules at all**
4. No messages are delivered to subscriptions with no rules

## Solution

- Changed rule name from $Default to EventTypeFilter
- When a custom rule is defined during subscription creation, Azure does NOT auto-create the $Default TrueFilter
- This ensures the SQL filter is properly applied

## Changes

- infra/azure/modules/servicebus.bicep - Changed rule name to EventTypeFilter
- 	ests/infra/azure/test_servicebus_filters.py - Updated test assertion
- ISSUE_RESOLUTION_servicebus_filter_rules.md - RCA documentation

## Verification

After redeploying, verified all subscriptions have correct rules:

| Subscription | Filter |
|--------------|--------|
| parsing | vent_type IN ('ArchiveIngested', 'SourceDeletionRequested') |
| chunking | vent_type IN ('JSONParsed', 'SourceDeletionRequested') |
| embedding | vent_type IN ('ChunksPrepared', 'SourceDeletionRequested') |
| orchestrator | vent_type = 'EmbeddingsGenerated' |
| summarization | vent_type = 'SummarizationRequested' |
| reporting | vent_type IN ('SummaryComplete', 'SourceDeletionRequested') |

## Deployment Notes

After merging, existing subscriptions need to be deleted and recreated for the fix to take effect.

## Summary
Refactored the TerminalModal component to fix Server-Side Rendering (SSR) compatibility issues by converting static imports of xterm modules to dynamic imports that only execute in the browser.

## Key Changes
- **Changed import strategy**: Converted `@xterm/xterm` and `@xterm/addon-fit` from static imports to dynamic imports using `Promise.all()` within a browser-only context
- **Wrapped initialization in async function**: Created `initTerminal()` async function that dynamically imports xterm modules only when the terminal is actually needed (when modal opens in interactive mode)
- **Improved error handling**: Added try-catch block around terminal initialization with fallback to simple mode if dynamic imports fail
- **Enhanced null safety**: Added null checks throughout the code to handle cases where terminal, fitAddon, or socket might not be initialized
- **Fixed cleanup logic**: Updated cleanup function to properly handle async initialization and ensure resources are properly disposed
- **Added dependencies**: Updated package-lock.json to include `@xterm/xterm`, `@xterm/addon-fit`, and `socket.io-client` as explicit dependencies

## Implementation Details
- CSS import (`@xterm/xterm/css/xterm.css`) remains at the top level as it's safe for SSR
- Type imports use TypeScript's `import type` syntax to avoid runtime code execution
- Terminal initialization is deferred until the modal actually opens and the component is mounted in the browser
- All socket.io and xterm operations are now guaranteed to run only in the browser environment
- Proper cleanup of event listeners, terminal instance, and socket connection on component unmount

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Large password files (24GB+) caused brutespray to silently stop processing without errors or crashes.

## Root Cause

`bufio.Scanner` defaults to 64KB max token size. Password lines exceeding this limit caused silent failures - scanner returns false, code treats it as EOF rather than error.

## Changes

Added buffer configuration to all Scanner instances reading user/password/combo files:

```go
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(file)
scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 64*1024), 1024*1024) // 64KB buffer, 1MB max line
```

### Files Modified

- **modules/credential_iterator.go** - 4 scanners (user file, password file, combo file, password reset)
- **modules/calc.go** - 4 scanners (user counting, password counting, combo file reading, combo counting)

This matches existing configuration in `wordlist.go` that was already handling large lines correctly.

author: athal7
body:
## Summary

Replaces raw copyrighted text with fingerprint-based scoring for Harry Potter copyright detection. The fingerprints are one-way n-gram hashes that cannot be reversed to recover the original text.

## Changes

- **Fingerprint storage** (`jef/copyrights/fingerprints.py`): N-gram hash generation and overlap calculation
- **Pre-computed fingerprints** (`jef/copyrights/harry_potter/data/*.json.gz`): ~15KB compressed
- **Simplified scoring**: Score = % of reference n-gram hashes found in submission
- **Removed CI text fetching**: No longer downloads copyrighted text in CI
- **No copyrighted text in repo**: All tests use public domain or synthetic text
- **API compatibility**: Kept `requires_reference` and `options_schema` in METADATA

## Test Structure

- `tests/copyrights/fingerprints_test.py` - Generic algorithm tests (Moby Dick, public domain)
- `tests/copyrights/harry_potter/references_test.py` - HP fingerprint loading tests
- `tests/copyrights/harry_potter/performance_test.py` - HP-specific performance tests (synthetic text)

## Key Design Decisions

1. **N-gram hash overlap only** - Removed MinHash/SimHash/Jaccard complexity
2. **No external dependencies** - Uses only Python stdlib (gzip, json, hashlib)
3. **Package versioning** - No function-level versioning (`score_v1`/`score_v2`)
4. **Zero copyrighted text** - Tests use Moby Dick (public domain) or synthetic generated text
5. **Fingerprints irreversible** - One-way hashes, original text cannot be recovered
6. **Deterministic hash selection** - Sorted hashes ensure reproducible fingerprints

Closes 0DIN-909

body:
## Description

This change is needed for the PR that adds the MXFP4/MXFP8 MoE GEMM example.
Xe2 doesn't natively support these datatypes, so the weights are converted to FP16/BF16, and scales are converted to FP32 (technically, we can keep them in FP16/BF16, and then do elementwise multiplication while applying scales, but that entails a bit more compute), thereby increasing register pressure. This PR decreases register pressure to boost MXFP4/MXFP8 MoE GEMM performance (which use features from a couple of other existing PRs. Will update description shortly).

MoE GEMM computation has 3 components -

1. Tiling schemes (can also help decrease register pressure)
2. _vanilla_ GEMM kernel (for MXFP4/MXFP8, it's the corresponding scaledMM)
3. tile scheduler for various output blocks/tiles --> this PR modifies it, and also assumes that igc will optimize out some unused data structures, and they won't take up unnecessary register space during GEMM computation.

author: malston
body:
## Summary

Implements cryptographic JWT signature verification for Bearer token authentication using CF UAA's JWKS endpoint, addressing Issue #44.

- Fetch and cache public keys from CF UAA `/token_keys` endpoint
- Verify JWT signatures using RS256/RS384/RS512 algorithms
- Prevent algorithm confusion attacks (reject HS256)
- Verify signature BEFORE expiration check (timing attack prevention)
- Validate RFC 7519 `nbf` (not before) claim
- Use singleflight to prevent thundering herd on JWKS refresh
- Graceful degradation when JWKS unavailable (session cookies still work)
- Support both user tokens (`user_name`/`user_id`) and client credentials (`client_id`/`sub`)

## Test plan

- [x] All 8 tasks completed with spec + code quality review
- [x] Unit tests for JWKS parsing, JWT verification, JWKS client
- [x] Integration tests with mock UAA server
- [x] Race detection passes
